correctness.rationale: The claim is restricted to the hull [0,1/m], not the complement in [0,1]. At a point's first escape, its preceding iterate y has a=floor(1/y)≥m and 1/m<T(y)<1 exactly when L_a<y<R_a. Pulling it back through the preceding digits gives the listed gap. Conversely each such interval escapes at the specified step; its endpoints survive since L_a maps to 0 and R_a to 1/m, which itself maps to 0. The first escape and its pre-escape digit identify the gap uniquely. This also gives an open complement in the hull and avoids any assumption of continuity of the Gauss map at rationals. Multiplying the inverse-branch Möbius matrices gives unit absolute determinant and denominator q_k+q_{k−1}t, so the length formula includes the empty prefix. The root lengths strictly decrease with a and every nonempty prefix satisfies |f_w(x)−f_w(y)|≤m^{−2|w|}|x−y|. The maximal normalized distance is thus m(R_m−L_m)/2, with the claimed limit. The nonterminating set is covered at depth j by intervals of total length at most (sum_{a≥m}a^{−2})^j/m, tending to zero since sum_{a≥2}a^{−2}<sum_{a≥2}1/[a(a−1)]=1. The terminating survivors are countable, so the disjoint gaps have total length 1/m.
residual_risks: The source's recorded finite rational checks are corroboration only and were not rerun; the first-escape and continuant arguments verify arbitrary digits, depths and thresholds in scope.
